group: walk – validation enabled (true) – valid instance

cases.expected: An empty Set – no validation messages because the instance conforms to the schema.
cases.description: The schema expects a required string property "name". The supplied node satisfies the schema, so walk should invoke the underlying validator and return an empty collection when validation is turned on.

group: walk – validation enabled (true) – invalid instance

cases.expected: A Set containing at least one ValidationMessage indicating a type error for property "name".
cases.description: The schema requires "name" to be a string, but the node provides a numeric value. With validation enabled, walk must run the type validator and return the corresponding validation message(s).

group: walk – validation disabled (false)

cases.expected: An empty Set – no validation messages because validation was skipped.
cases.description: When the validate flag is false, walk must bypass all validators and return an empty result regardless of the node content.

group: walk – null JsonNode

cases.expected: NullPointerException
cases.description: The implementation expects a non‑null JsonNode. Supplying null should cause a NullPointerException before any validation logic is executed.

group: walk – null OutputFormat

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException (or NullPointerException) indicating that outputFormat must not be null
cases.description: The method should guard against a null OutputFormat because it is required to produce a result. The expected behaviour is to throw an exception immediately.

group: walk – node is an array (schema expects object)

cases.expected: A Set containing a ValidationMessage about the instance type mismatch (expected OBJECT, found ARRAY).
cases.description: The schema is defined for an object with a required property "name". Providing an array should trigger the type validator and produce an appropriate error message.

group: walk – schema with recursive anchor (isRecursiveAnchor = true)

cases.expected: A Set without infinite recursion – validation completes successfully (or contains only expected messages for the concrete instance).
cases.description: When the schema contains a recursive anchor, walk must detect and handle recursion correctly, avoiding a StackOverflowError. The test verifies that the method returns a finite result.

group: walk – validation enabled (true) – missing required property

cases.expected: A Set containing a ValidationMessage indicating that required property "name" is missing.
cases.description: The schema declares "name" as required. Supplying an empty object should cause the required‑property validator to emit a message when validation is enabled.

group: walk – validation enabled (true) – additionalProperties false

cases.expected: A Set containing a ValidationMessage that property "age" is not allowed (additionalProperties = false).
cases.description: The schema defines only the property "name" and sets "additionalProperties": false. An extra property should be flagged by the additional‑properties validator.

group: walk – validation enabled (true) – enum violation

cases.expected: A Set containing a ValidationMessage that value "unknown" is not one of the allowed enum values ["active","inactive"].
cases.description: The schema adds an enum constraint on property "status". Providing a value outside the enum should produce an enum‑validation error.

group: walk – validation enabled (true) – pattern mismatch

cases.expected: A Set containing a ValidationMessage that string "not-an-email" does not match the regex pattern "^[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\\.[A-Za-z]{2,}$" for property "email".
cases.description: The schema defines a regex pattern for an email address. Supplying a non‑matching string should trigger the pattern validator.

group: walk – validation enabled (true) – numeric range violation (minimum)

cases.expected: A Set containing a ValidationMessage that numeric value -5 is less than the allowed minimum 0 for property "age".
cases.description: The schema specifies a minimum of 0 for the numeric property "age". Providing a negative number should be reported by the numeric‑range validator.

group: walk – validation enabled (true) – array length violation (minItems)

cases.expected: A Set containing a ValidationMessage that array "tags" has fewer items (0) than the required minimum of 1.
cases.description: The schema defines "tags" as an array with "minItems": 1. An empty array should be flagged by the array‑size validator.

group: walk – $ref to external schema – valid instance

cases.expected: An empty Set – the referenced address schema validates the supplied address object successfully.
cases.description: The main schema contains a "$ref": "address-schema.json#". The provided address object conforms to the external schema, so no validation messages are expected.

group: walk – $ref to external schema – invalid instance

cases.expected: A Set containing at least two ValidationMessages: one for type mismatch on "street" (expected string, found integer) and one for pattern/minLength violation on "zip" (value "12" does not satisfy the zip‑code pattern).
cases.description: The referenced external schema expects "street" to be a string and "zip" to match a five‑digit pattern. Supplying an integer and a too‑short zip should generate appropriate messages.

group: walk – $ref with URL‑encoded fragment

cases.expected: An empty Set – the URL‑decoded fragment resolves to the "name" property schema, which validates the supplied string value.
cases.description: The $ref contains an URL‑encoded JSON‑Pointer. The walk method must decode it correctly before locating the target schema.

group: walk – boolean schema true (accept any instance)

cases.expected: An empty Set – a schema defined as the boolean literal true accepts any JSON value without producing messages.
cases.description: When the root schema is the boolean true, walk should short‑circuit validation and return an empty result irrespective of the instance.

group: walk – boolean schema false (reject any instance)

cases.expected: A Set containing a single ValidationMessage indicating that the instance is invalid because the schema is false.
cases.description: A schema defined as the boolean false must cause every instance to be considered invalid, resulting in a generic validation error.

group: walk – instance type mismatch (scalar vs object)

cases.expected: A Set containing a ValidationMessage that the instance type is STRING but the schema expects OBJECT.
cases.description: The schema is defined for an object with required property "name". Supplying a plain string should trigger the type validator.

group: walk – outputFormat throws RuntimeException

cases.expected: IllegalStateException (or any RuntimeException) propagated from the OutputFormat implementation
cases.description: A custom OutputFormat is supplied whose collect method deliberately throws an IllegalStateException. The walk method should not swallow this exception; it must propagate it to the caller.

group: walk – $ref to non‑existent fragment

cases.expected: JsonSchemaException (or IllegalArgumentException) indicating that the $ref fragment could not be resolved
cases.description: The schema contains a $ref that points to a JSON‑Pointer that does not exist in the current schema. The walk method must detect the unresolved reference and throw an exception rather than returning a normal result.

group: walk – schema with unsupported keyword causing IllegalStateException

cases.expected: IllegalStateException (or JsonSchemaException) stating that an unknown validator/keyword was encountered
cases.description: A schema is constructed that contains an unknown keyword (e.g., "x‑unknownKeyword": true). When walk processes this schema it should fail fast with an IllegalStateException because it cannot map the unknown keyword to a validator.
